::: {.remark .notes}

Hoeffding stated the inequality for sums of independent bounded random variables, with different bounds for each term [@hoeffding1963].
This page states the case of the sample mean of IID variables in $[0, 1]$,
which is the case that bounds the gap between a sample proportion and the probability it estimates.
For an indicator variable, $\mean$ is the probability of the event and $\samplemean{X}{n}$ is the share of the $n$ draws in which it occurs.

:::
